name: Czech Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language; no published description of word stress found (Glottolog refs are classification/endangerment only).

sources.citation: Charles University repository (dspace.cuni.cz) searches: fonologie / prozodie / přízvuk / důraz / nemanuální / fonetika + (český) znakový jazyk; Crossref bibliographic queries 'Czech Sign Language', 'český znakový jazyk'
sources.tag: read: notes on stress
sources.note: No thesis or article on prosody, stress, rhythm or intonation of ČZJ surfaced; hits are on parameters (handshape, passive hand, minimal pairs), mouthings/oral components, negation, aspect, notation.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page czec1253 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.tag: read: notes on stress

sources.tag: read: notes on stress

sources.citation: Langer, Jiří, Jan Andres, Martina Benešová & Dan Faltýnek. 2020. Quantitative Linguistic Analysis of Czech Sign Language. Olomouc: Palacký University. 196 pp. DOI 10.5507/pdf.20.24457277
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Sec. 1.3 'Sign language as a natural language' (pp. 25-27) describes ČZJ sign phonology as five simultaneous parameters (place, handshape, palm/finger orientation, hand arrangement, movement, after Macurová 1996 and Souralová 2004) and then non-manual factors; no mention of stress, accent or prominence at sign or phrase level (a full-text search for stress/accent/prosod/rhythm finds only non-technical uses).

sources.citation: Klabanová, Lucie. 2012. Vizuální percepce a fonologické formy lexémů českého znakového jazyka (frekvenční analýza vybraných parametrů znaků). BA thesis, Charles University. 102 pp.
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Frequency analysis of handshape and location in ČZJ signs; no mention of stress, prosody or rhythm.

sources.citation: Okrouhlíková, Lenka. 2012. Notace – zápis českého znakového jazyka. PhD dissertation, Charles University, Faculty of Education. 334 pp.
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Notation systems for ČZJ manual and non-manual components (sec. 4.3 non-manual notation, p. 198, notes no inventory of ČZJ non-manual components exists); 'přízvuk' occurs only as the name of diacritic accent marks in a notation; nothing on sign stress.

sources.citation: Silovská, Zuzana. 2012. Minimální páry v českém znakovém jazyce. BA thesis, Charles University, Prague (sup. K. Richterová). 206 pp.
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Phonology thesis on minimal pairs by parameter; 'přízvuk'/'suprasegmentální' appear only in the general definition of the phoneme quoted from Čermák 2004 (spoken-language intonation and stress); nothing on stress in ČZJ.

sources.citation: Mareš, Jindřich. 2011. Orální komponenty v českém znakovém jazyce. BA thesis, Charles University. 94 pp.
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Oral components (mouth gestures); notes their 'intenzita a rytmus' follow the manual movement's intensity and rhythm; nothing on word/sign stress.

sources.citation: Motejzíková, Jitka. 2007. Simultánnost v českém znakovém jazyce. MA thesis, Charles University (sup. A. Macurová). 117 pp.
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Simultaneity of manual and non-manual components; mentions body/head moving 'v rytmu pohybu rukou' (in the rhythm of the hand movement) and spoken-Czech intonation as suprasegmental; nothing on stress or prominence in ČZJ.
